issues.description: The problem statement uses a snake_case method name `get_total_number_of_students()` (problem_statement.md) while the UML, template comments, and the solution use the Java-style camelCase method name `getTotalNumberOfStudents()`. This naming/signature inconsistency can confuse students about the exact method to implement and cause mismatches with automated tests that expect the camelCase name.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the problem statement to consistently use the camelCase method name getTotalNumberOfStudents() everywhere (replace `get_total_number_of_students()`), so it matches the UML, template hints, and the solution. Ensure any example/test references also use the same camelCase name.

issues.description: The problem statement uses a snake_case name get_total_number_of_students() (line 40) while the UML, the template comments, and the solution implementation use the camelCase name getTotalNumberOfStudents(). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual method (total number of students) can confuse students about the exact method they are expected to implement in Java, where camelCase is the norm.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the occurrence in problem_statement.md from get_total_number_of_students() to getTotalNumberOfStudents() (camelCase) so it matches the UML, template comments, and the solution implementation. Alternatively, add a brief note in the problem text stating that method names should follow Java camelCase conventions and that getTotalNumberOfStudents() is the expected name.
